thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: metering-anomaly detected for production token counts (alert id: MTR-4492). Spike in token emit rate for multiple customers since 11:07 UTC. Triggering rule: token_count > baseline * 3.

raj: Acknowledging. I'm oncall. Starting triage — where's the first signal?

amanda: billing-bot ran the hourly ingestion alert. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/metering/exp and there's a clear step up at 11:07 for the ingest-emit pipeline (shard 7). Sample customer IDs: cust_42, cust_99, cust_314.

chris: I see matching runtime traces. A flurry of duplicate `emit_usage` requests from the metering-proxy to ingress between 11:07:02 and 11:07:08. Suspect the proxy retried without idempotency keys.

amanda: That matches why overage flags started firing downstream. CS already got two automated overage emails. We should suppress customer-facing overage notifications until we confirm root cause.

sara: Agree. Action: temp-suppress notifications, open mitigation window. I'm going to run the suppression flag.

lex: @sara please include support so we can notify affected customers with an honest blameless note once we have a mitigated state. I have the partial list: cust_42 (prod), cust_99 (staging->prod mixed traffic), cust_314 (prod). Estimated impacted accounts: ~18 by quick query.

billing-bot: Automated recon summary: 
- total tokens emitted in window: 68,412,312 (expected baseline: 19,230,145)
- customers with >2x increase: 18
- potential overcharge window: 11:07:02 - 11:14:30 UTC

raj: Good catch. Immediate steps: 1) suppress overage emails; 2) block replay/duplicate emits at ingress; 3) roll revert or patch to proxy if needed; 4) backfill reconciliation plan. Assigning owners: sara (suppress + backpressure), chris (proxy triage + patch), amanda (billing reconciliation + customer list), lex (CS comms).

sara: Running command to flip flag: 
```
POST https://internal-api.redwood/flags/metering/suppress_overage_notifications
Body: { "reason": "incident MTR-4492 - spike suspected duplicates", "expires_in": "2h" }
```
Response: 200 OK. Notifications suppressed. :white_check_mark:

chris: Replicating issue locally. Logs: 
```
[11:07:03] proxy-7 INFO: upstream 10.12.8.7 responded 504, retrying request idempotent=false
[11:07:04] proxy-7 WARN: missing idempotency-key header for request /emit-usage
[11:07:04] proxy-7 INFO: forwarded request to ingress-3
[11:07:05] proxy-7 INFO: upstream 10.12.8.7 responded 200, but original also eventually succeeded => duplicate
```
Root cause hypothesis: a transient 504 from ingress + proxy behavior that retries non-idempotent endpoints. There's no dedupe on metering ingest.

amanda: Can we block writes with duplicate request signatures (customer+traceid+timestamp) at the metering-processor for a quick mitigation? Even a short-lived dedupe layer would fix counts.

chris: I can add a soft dedupe path in the proxy routing layer: if `idempotency-key` missing, treat as unique but set `dedupe-key` based on (customer_id, request_hash) and check Redis TTL 5s. Implementing now on canary.

sara: While chris works on that, I'm applying backpressure to proxies to reduce burst: `kubectl scale deployment/proxy --replicas=0` is too heavy. I'm setting a rate-limit rule on ingress-nginx config to 50r/s per shard. Pushing rule: `ingress/metric-ingress -> rate-limit=50`.

oncall-pager: Deploy job started: `deploy/proxy-dedupe-canary` (build 2026.3.18-213). Rolling one pod on shard 7.

amanda: Billing reconciliation plan: pause billing exports for the suspect window and start a queued backfill that will dedupe by event_id if available. If dedupe not possible, we'll compute median baseline and credit affected customers. Need agreement on policy for credits.

lex: CS note draft (for internal review): "We observed an internal metering duplication leading to inflated usage for a subset of customers between 11:07–11:14 UTC. We've suppressed automated notifications, and are currently reconciling usage. We'll follow up within 2 hours with next steps and any automatic credits."

raj: Good. Chime in with severity: Sev2 (customer impact, automated emails suppressed). Keep paging channel open. ETA for chris patch?

chris: Canary is up on shard 7. Initial telemetry looks promising — duplicate emit rate down ~95% for that shard in the 30s window after canary. Logs show dedupe check hitting Redis and dropping duplicates: 
```
[11:10:12] proxy-dedupe-canary INFO: dedupe key hit for (cust_314, reqhash=0x9f3a) -> drop
```
I'll roll canary to two more shards in 10m if stable.

amanda: Billing snapshot: pausing exports to downstream billing-sink for the window. Starting a backfill worker with dedupe logic (prefer event_id then request_hash). Kicking off job: `billing-backfill --window start=1768234022 end=1768234470 --dedupe=true`

sara: Rate limit applied across shards. System CPU load stable. No other regressions seen.

lex: CS: prepping outbound email about mitigation (internal first). Running list of top 5 customers to prioritize. Will hold public comms until recon finishes.

billing-bot: Backfill job progress: 10% processed (eta 45m). Current dedupe savings estimate: ~52% of extra tokens will be removed by dedupe; remainder likely genuine spike.

raj: Action items recap (from thread):
- [sara] suppress notifications (done) and apply rate-limit (done)
- [chris] deploy dedupe canary and roll if stable (in progress)
- [amanda] pause exports, run backfill dedupe (in progress)
- [lex] CS comms draft and prioritize customers (in progress)
- [raj] monitor and decide on automatic credits policy in 2 hours based on backfill results

sara: I'm opening a follow-up postmortem ticket: PM-1789 and linking this thread. Please add any notes.

chris: Canary rolled to all affected shards at 11:22 UTC. Duplicate emit alerts have returned to baseline. Will keep monitoring.

amanda: Backfill complete at 11:58 UTC. Reconciliation numbers: final tokens after dedupe: 22,034,876 (baseline 19.23M). Over-count above baseline: ~2.8M tokens across 18 customers. Preliminary credit policy: auto-credit 100% of tokens beyond baseline for customers with >50% of their spike deduped; manual review for others. Need biz sign-off.

lex: CS reviewed and okayed the customer messaging for auto-credit for the clearly duplicated ones. Preparing outbound.

raj: Thanks all. Severity -> reduced to Sev4 at 12:05 UTC. Incident resolved operationally; billing reconciliation and CS comms remain follow-ups. Leaving thread open for audit and the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident MTR-4492 resolved (reduced severity). Postmortem ticket: PM-1789.

lex: Closing note: customers affected: 18, estimated auto-credits to issue: ~2.8M tokens (applied nightly job). No customer has been involuntarily charged yet because we paused exports.

sara: Adding a mitigation playbook update: require `Idempotency-Key` header validation at proxy and dedupe TTL of 10s for metering endpoints.

chris: I'll open a change request to make the dedupe permanent. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
